pass_a_gloss: (The wrestling) then is for us against authorities not visible and fleshly, and world-rulers of the darkness surrounding the human race, and against the spirits of wickedness inhabiting the heavenly place, that is the air; and in other places at least he said 'in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit now working in the (sons of) disobedience'. For the air poured around us seems to have been filled with opposing powers. Eph 6:13 'that you may be able to withstand', he says, 'in the evil day.' [Origen:] the one seeking to withstand in the evil day ought to have the full armor of God which the apostle set out, through which the one from the opposite side will be shamed, having nothing base to say about us, the devil and accuser of our brothers and deceiving the sinners as his own and as having become of his portion. Another will say the present age is an evil day. And a third account besides the two interpretations will be one saying that the contest has no end for the one who has gone out of this life, but that even the one who conquered here is going to contend in another evil day also against the opposing energies appearing. [6:14] 'stand therefore having girded your loins in truth.' And in the Gospel according to Luke it is written 'let your loins be girded'. And what the belt is now we know: the one who has contracted the matters of generation and no longer serves it but hastens to immortality girds the loins. [6:14] 'and having put on the breastplate of righteousness.' Just as the one who has put on a breastplate is less vulnerable when shot by enemies, and especially less vulnerable in the more vital parts, so the one clothed in righteousness would not be wounded, not even as a deer struck by an arrow into the liver; for he will fall neither into anger nor into desire, but will also remain pure in heart, by having put on the breastplate of righteousness forged for him by the craftsman of all, God, who having prepared it gives the full armor to each of the saints. [6:15] 'and having shod the feet in readiness of the gospel of peace.' Observe that he named a certain power of the soul feet, with which as it were we journey, walking the one who said 'I am the way', which must be shod with the readiness of the gospel of peace. And I think the shoes recorded in Exodus are symbols of these shoes, which those eating the Passover and being ready for the journey had to have. For thus he says: 'thus you shall eat it: your loins girded and your shoes on your feet and your staffs in your hands, and you shall eat it with haste; it is the Lord's Passover.' For both eating with haste and eating having been shod belong to readiness, so that being strengthened by the food they may be able to journey. So let the one journeying be shod, but the one who has arrived at the holy land be unshod; for 'loose', it says, 'the shoe from your feet, for the place in which you stand is holy ground.' Therefore let the non-apostle be shod as to the feet in readiness of the gospel of peace; but let the apostle no longer take shoes for a road, having already been perfected and being in the place where, both standing and walking, he is on holy ground, living in Christ. Eph 6:16 ['in all things having taken up the shield of faith, in which you will be able to quench all the fiery arrows of the evil one.'] [Origen says:] the arrows of the evil one are the evil reasonings; so he will not even be able to cast at the start into the heart whenever someone is covered by the shield of faith, all the fiery arrows of the enemy being quenched in it. And the one who has put on the shield of faith will say 'in the Lord I have trusted; how will you say to my soul, migrate to the mountains as a sparrow? for behold the sinners stretched a bow, they prepared arrows in a quiver, to shoot in a moonless night the upright in heart.' For since I have trusted, he says, in the Lord, how do you counsel me not to stand against the bows being stretched against me by the sinners and the arrows being prepared by them in quivers, they wishing to wound the upright in heart? For behold I both stand and do not migrate, and all the fiery arrows of the evil one will all but be quenched. [6:17b, 18, 19a] 'and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, through all prayer and petition, praying in every season in spirit, and being watchful unto it in all perseverance and' (continues)
pass_b_english: is, then, against authorities that are not visible or made of flesh; against world rulers of the darkness that surrounds the human race; and against the spirits of wickedness that dwell in the heavenly place, that is, the air. Elsewhere, at any rate, he said, "in which you once walked, according to the course of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now at work in the [sons of] disobedience" (Ephesians 2:2). For the air poured around us seems to be filled with opposing powers.

"So that you may be able to withstand," he says, "in the evil day" (Ephesians 6:13). Origen: Whoever seeks to withstand in the evil day must have the whole armor of God that the apostle set out. Because of it the opponent will be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us (Titus 2:8): the devil, the accuser of our brothers (Revelation 12:10), who deceives sinners as his own, as men who have come to belong to his portion. Another will say that the present age is the evil day. A third interpretation, besides these two, will say that the struggle has no end for the one who has left this life: even the one who has conquered here will have to contend in another evil day against the opposing forces that appear.

"Stand, therefore, having girded your waist with truth" (Ephesians 6:14). In Luke too it is written, "Let your waists be girded" (Luke 12:35). We know what the belt is here: the one who has curbed the business of begetting, and no longer serves it but hastens toward immortality, girds his waist.

"And having put on the breastplate of righteousness" (Ephesians 6:14). The one who has put on a breastplate is harder to hurt when enemies shoot at him, and hardest to hurt in the vital parts. In the same way the one clothed with righteousness could not be wounded, not even like a deer struck by an arrow in the liver. For he will fall neither into rage nor into desire, but will remain pure in heart, because he has put on the breastplate of righteousness forged for him by God, the craftsman of all things, who makes the whole armor for each of the saints and gives it to him.

"And having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace" (Ephesians 6:15). Observe that he has called a certain power of the soul "feet," with which, as it were, we travel, walking along the one who said, "I am the way" (John 14:6). These must be shod with the readiness of the gospel of peace. I think the shoes recorded in Exodus are symbols of these shoes, the ones that those who ate the Passover had to wear, being ready for the journey. For it says, "This is how you shall eat it: your waists girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is the Lord's Passover" (Exodus 12:11). Both eating in haste and eating with shoes on belong to readiness, so that, strengthened by the food, they might be able to travel. So let the one who is traveling be shod, and let the one who has reached the holy land take his shoes off. For it says, "Take off the shoe from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground" (Exodus 3:5). For this reason, let the one who is not an apostle have his feet shod with the readiness of the gospel of peace. But let the apostle no longer take shoes for the road, since he has already been made perfect and is in the place where, standing and walking, he is on holy ground, living in Christ.

"In all things taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the evil one" (Ephesians 6:16). Origen says: The arrows of the evil one are evil thoughts. So he will not be able even to begin to cast them into the heart when someone is covered by the shield of faith, since all the enemy's flaming arrows are quenched in it. And the one who carries the shield of faith will say, "In the Lord I have put my trust. How can you say to my soul, 'Flee to the mountains like a sparrow'? For look, the sinners have bent the bow; they have made ready arrows in the quiver, to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart" (Psalm 11:1-2). "Since I have put my trust in the Lord," he says, "how can you advise me not to stand up to the bows that sinners bend against me, and the arrows they make ready in quivers, wanting to wound the upright in heart? For look, I stand, and I do not move away, and all the flaming arrows of the evil one will be quenched any moment now."

The Greek on disk lacks υἱοῖς; the Ephesians 2:2 wording supplies it; bracketed as a restoration.
